messages.subject: Mediation analysis
parts:
Hello,

I am trying to run a mediation analysis in lavaan but ran into problems.

My model includes "maltreatment" as X, 3 binary mediators (condnone, conddisr and condoppos) who have  been dummy-coded from a 3-class categorical variable, and "controlrestr" as Y.

My syntax is:

model <- '
+ controlrestr~c*maltreatment
+ condnone~a*maltreatment
+ conddisr~a*maltreatment
+ condoppos~a*maltreatment
+ controlrestr~b*condnone
+ controlrestr~b*conddisr
+ controlrestr~b*condoppos
+ ab:=a*b
+ total:=c+(a*b)
'
fit<-sem(model,data=datashort,group="sex",test="bootstrap")

When I run the "fit" function, I get the following error message: ERROR: subscript out of bounds

Can anyone tell me what this might be about ?

Thanks,

David Joubert

I'm not sure why you get this specific error message. Would you be able
to send me a snippet of the data (together with your R script) so I can
replicate this?

But more importantly: since your mediators are binary, you need to treat
them as binary variables. Unfortunately, the current version of lavaan
(0.5-9) does not allow (yet) to use bootstrapping if either the outcome
or the mediators are categorical. This will be fixed in 0.5-10.

Yves.

> fit<-sem(model,data=datashort,group="sex",ordered=c("conddisr","condoppos","controlrestr"))

I had some time to study this problem, and it turns out that the problem
is due to the sparse two-way table for the two variables controlrestr
and conddisr in the sex==0 group:


> with(subset(datashort, sex==0), table(controlrestr, conddisr))
conddisr
controlrestr 1 2
1 97 6
2 3 0

Not only is there a zero cell (always problematic in the bivariate
case), most cases are in the (1,1) cell, leading to an estimated
correlation of almost (-)1.0.

If there were no independent variables, the typical 'fix' would be to
add a small value to the empty cell. However, in your setup, there is an
independent variable (maltreatment), and it is (to me) unclear how to
'fix' this. But perhaps, it is better to merge the conddisr and
controlrestr variables, since they seem to overlap almost completely (at
least in this group).

Yves.
